objective: Re-run the Phase-100 contract-vs-spec fidelity screen on a HARDER corpus where bare prompts plausibly FAIL — real, challenging code-development tasks grounded in edge-screener (a backtesting platform whose whole thesis is un-foolable integrity tests: no-lookahead, costs, survivorship). The Phase-100 null was ceiling-saturated (capable worker aced toy tasks); this directly attacks that limitation by giving the contract structure failure headroom to demonstrate (or not) fidelity lift on subtle-integrity tasks.
recommendation: GATE CLOSED. Maintainer chose FROM-SCRATCH STUB (B) over bug-injection: stub a real integrity-critical FUNCTION in edge-screener (a single function with one strong, namable invariant — e.g. the decision-lag weights[k] earn returns[k+1], or cost application, or PIT survivorship), the worker re-implements it; bare = 'implement function X to do Y'; spec = + objectives prose; contract = + the named integrity invariant as a deterministic guardrail (test file HELD-OUT). Score with edge-screener's un-foolable held-out integrity tests + the cross-model judge. Function-level stubs (not whole modules) to keep floor risk manageable. CRUX (A1 accept): a MANDATORY difficulty-calibration pilot keeps only tasks where bare FAILS but isn't floored; if none land in-band, the phase reports an informative null ('no discriminating harder corpus constructible for this worker'). Reuses the frozen Phase-100 harness.

options.label: A — Bug-injection-repair + calibration pilot (held-out integrity tests)
options.description: Inject a subtle integrity bug into a working edge-screener module; the worker fixes it. The contract names the integrity invariant (no-lookahead / costs / survivorship) as a guardrail without the test file; held-out integrity tests score. Localized fix = best-calibrated (the worker has a working base; the contract's value is naming the invariant a bare prompt overlooks). A mandatory pilot discards floor/ceiling tasks before freezing.

options.label: B — From-scratch stub-a-module
options.description: Remove a real integrity-critical module; the worker re-implements it from the prompt; held-out integrity tests score. Cleaner 'fresh implementation' but HIGH floor risk — re-implementing a no-lookahead backtest engine from scratch may fail on ALL arms (too hard) → no discrimination.

options.label: C — Mine real git-history regressions
options.description: Reconstruct real bugs from edge-screener's git history (authentic regressions a contract might have prevented). Most realistic, but heavy setup (pre-fix state + the fix's test per task) and harder to calibrate to the discrimination band.

assumptions.text: Tasks can be calibrated to the DISCRIMINATION BAND — bare fails but isn't floored (a contract has room to help) — verified by a MANDATORY difficulty-calibration pilot BEFORE freezing the corpus. If no task lands in-band (all floor or all ceiling), the phase reports an informative null ('no discriminating harder corpus constructible'), not a forced contract-vs-spec conclusion.

Bug-injection-repair is the right construction (a localized fix to a working module — the contract's value is naming the integrity invariant the bare worker overlooks), vs from-scratch stub (floor risk) or git-mining (setup-heavy).

The worker can develop + be scored in a real edge-screener copy (its .venv/deps work, opencode can run pytest there), at a heavier per-run cost than Phase 100 → a smaller corpus (3-4 tasks x n=3-5). Feasibility verified in the pilot; if the env can't run, re-scope.
edge-screener is the right base project (real, genuinely hard, un-foolable integrity tests, the maintainer's domain) vs an alternative codebase or synthetic-but-hard tasks.

context.active_phase: Phase 100 — Contract-vs-Spec Fidelity Screen DELIVERED (amplifier-null → collapse-to-runner-only; ceiling-saturated corpus). Phase 101 = the harder-corpus follow-on routed forward.
open_decisions: A1 (the crux): can a discriminating harder corpus even be constructed for this worker? — a pilot answers it; a clean 'no' is itself a result.
Reuses the frozen Phase-100 harness (runner/check/analyze/judge); the new design is the corpus + the worker-in-edge-screener workspace.
The contract's guardrails = edge-screener's integrity invariants named as deterministic checks; the actual test files stay HELD-OUT (Phase-100 keystone) so a worker can't iterate-to-green.
